source.title: Some open problems related to stability

accepted.question_text: Consider the multi-server first-come-first-served queue G/G/m with interarrival times {(t_n)} and service times {(sigma_n)} such that the two-dimensional sequence {(sigma_n, t_n)} is stationary ergodic, the stability condition E sigma_1 < m E t_1 holds, and the Kiefer-Wolfowitz workload vector starts from the zero initial value. Is it true that, under these assumptions alone and without any further mixing or regenerative condition, the distribution of the workload vector converges in total variation to a stationary distribution as n tends to infinity?
accepted.context_brief: TV convergence in stationary ergodic G/G/m FCFS

evidence.quote: The conjecture is: assuming only that the sequence {(sigma_n, t_n)} is stationary ergodic, that the stability condition holds, and that the initial value is 0, then there is no need for any further restriction to establish the convergence in the total variation.
sup_A |P(W_n in A) - pi(A)| -> 0, n -> infinity.

accepted.question_text: Let D be the stationary waiting time in an i.i.d. G/G/m first-come-first-served queue where the service-time sequence {(sigma_n)} and interarrival-time sequence {(t_n)} are independent, identically distributed, and satisfy rho := E sigma_1 / E t_1 < m. When rho is an integer, what conditions are necessary and sufficient for the power moment E D^gamma to be finite?
accepted.context_brief: Moments of stationary delay at integer load

evidence.quote: Assume now that {sigma_n} and {t_n} are two i.i.d. sequences that do not depend on each other. Continue to assume the stability condition rho := E sigma_1/E t_1 < m holds. Recall that in this case the stationary distribution is unique. Denote by D the stationary waiting time in the multi-server queue.
An open problem here is: what are the conditions for existence (finiteness) of power moments of D if rho is an integer.

accepted.question_text: In the two-server queue case m = 2 with stationary waiting time D, when the load satisfies rho = 1 and the service-time distribution is subexponential (for example regularly varying), what is the asymptotic behavior of P(D > x) as x becomes large?
accepted.context_brief: Tail asymptotics for two-server queue at rho=1

evidence.quote: Again let D be the stationary waiting time. We formulate the following questions: what may the asymptotics for P(D > x) be when x is large and what is the typical sample path which lead to such a large value of the stationary waiting time.

The open problems here are (I formulate them in the particular case of a two server queue, m = 2): find the asymptotics for P(D > x) (i) if rho = 1 - at least, for some particular subexponential (say, regularly varying) distribution of service times;

accepted.question_text: In the two-server queue case m = 2 with stationary waiting time D, when the load satisfies rho in (1, 2) and the service-time distribution is heavy-tailed but has all power moments finite, for example P(sigma_1 > x) = exp(-x^beta) for some beta in (0, 1), what is the asymptotic behavior of P(D > x) as x becomes large?
accepted.context_brief: Tail asymptotics for two-server queue with finite moments

evidence.quote: Again let D be the stationary waiting time. We formulate the following questions: what may the asymptotics for P(D > x) be when x is large and what is the typical sample path which lead to such a large value of the stationary waiting time.
The open problems here are (I formulate them in the particular case of a two server queue, m = 2): find the asymptotics for P(D > x)
(ii) if rho in (1, 2) and if the distribution of service times is heavy-tailed but has all power moments finite, for example, if P(sigma_1 > x) = e^{-x^beta}, for some beta in (0, 1).

accepted.question_text: In a two-server queue with stationary waiting time D, what are the typical sample paths that lead to large values of D in the following rare-event regimes: rho = 1 with a subexponential service-time distribution such as a regularly varying distribution, and rho in (1, 2) with a heavy-tailed service-time distribution that has all power moments finite, for example P(sigma_1 > x) = exp(-x^beta) for some beta in (0, 1)?
accepted.context_brief: Typical paths producing large stationary delays

evidence.quote: Again let D be the stationary waiting time. We formulate the following questions: what may the asymptotics for P(D > x) be when x is large and what is the typical sample path which lead to such a large value of the stationary waiting time.
It would be great to understand what are in these cases the typical paths which lead to large values of D.

accepted.question_text: Consider a multi-server queue, for example a two-server queue, with stationary ergodic input {(t_n, sigma_n)} and the join-the-shortest-queue discipline, meaning each arriving customer immediately joins the shortest of the individual queues. Assuming only the obvious stability condition and no extra hypotheses, how many stationary regimes can this model have?
accepted.context_brief: Number of stationary regimes for join-the-shortest-queue

evidence.quote: Consider again the multi-server (say, 2-server) queue with stationary and ergodic input {t_n, sigma_n}, but assume now that the discipline is join-the-shortest-queue: there are individual queues in front of the servers, and each arriving customer joins immediately the shortest queue (or one of the shortest at random if there are many).
So, here are the open problems: how many stationary regimes may exist if we do not assume any extra condition in addition to the obvious stability condition?

accepted.question_text: Consider a multi-server queue, for example a two-server queue, with stationary ergodic input {(t_n, sigma_n)} and individual queues in front of the servers, where each arriving customer immediately joins the shortest queue or chooses among tied shortest queues at random. What are the minimal assumptions that guarantee uniqueness of the stationary regime?

evidence.quote: Consider again the multi-server (say, 2-server) queue with stationary and ergodic input {t_n, sigma_n}, but assume now that the discipline is join-the-shortest-queue.
So, here are the open problems: what are the minimal requirements for the uniqueness of the stationary regime?

accepted.question_text: Consider a multi-server queue, for example a two-server queue, with stationary ergodic input {(t_n, sigma_n)} and individual queues in front of the servers, where each arriving customer immediately joins the shortest queue or chooses among tied shortest queues at random. Under what conditions, if any, do the queue-length or workload distributions converge weakly or in total variation to stationarity?

evidence.quote: Consider again the multi-server (say, 2-server) queue with stationary and ergodic input {t_n, sigma_n}, but assume now that the discipline is join-the-shortest-queue: there are individual queues in front of the servers, and each arriving customer joins immediately the shortest queue (or one of the shortest at random if there are many).
So, here are the open problems: under what conditions (none?) do we have weak (or TV) convergence?
The model exhibits NO monotonicity. It is not amenable to Loynes-type schemes. It is entirely open.

accepted.question_text: A single server moves on a circle. Particles arrive according to a Poisson process of rate lambda and are placed uniformly on the circle. Serving a particle takes one unit of time, and after each service the server moves at positive finite constant speed to the nearest waiting particle, ignoring new arrivals while moving. Is this greedy-server model stable for every lambda < 1?
accepted.context_brief: Stability of a greedy server on a circle

evidence.quote: A single server is located on the circle. Particles arrive in a Poisson stream of rate lambda and are uniformly distributed on the circle. It takes a single unit of time to serve a particle. After any service, the particle disappears, the server chooses to serve next the closest particle and moves to it with a positive finite constant speed.
The conjecture is: this model is stable for any lambda < 1.

accepted.question_text: On a circle, black particles arrive according to a Poisson stream of rate lambda and remain there, while white particles arrive according to an independent Poisson stream of rate 1 and immediately disappear after, if possible, deleting the nearest black particle within distance epsilon of their arrival location. Is this model stable whenever lambda < 1, independently of the circle length and of epsilon?
accepted.context_brief: Stability of black-white particle circle model

evidence.quote: Again, there is a circle, but this time no server or service. Instead, there are two independent Poisson streams/rains, of black and of white particles, with rates lambda and 1, respectively. Black particles arrive at the circle and stop there, but white particles pass straight through the circle. There is given a distance epsilon > 0. When a white particle passes through the circle at some point, it observes all blacks in the epsilon-neighbourhood and takes the one which is the closest to itself.
The natural conjecture is: stability should be guaranteed by the condition lambda < 1, independently of the circle length and the number epsilon. But the problem is open too.

accepted.question_text: Consider the following queueing system. There are three servers and a Poisson arrival process of rate lambda. Each arrival becomes class 1, 2, or 3 with probability 1/3. Class 1 customers may be served by servers 1 and 2, class 2 customers by servers 2 and 3, and class 3 customers by servers 3 and 1. Upon arrival, a customer chooses the accessible server with the shorter workload. If served by its left server, the service time has distribution F_l; if served by its right server, the service time has distribution F_r. Can the stability conditions for this system depend both on the initial values and on the whole service-time distributions F_l and F_r?

evidence.quote: Consider a system with three servers (numbered 1 to 3) fed by a Poisson process with intensity lambda. There are three classes of customers and each arriving customer becomes a class i customer (i = 1, 2, 3) with probability 1/3.

Upon arrival, a customer chooses an accessible server with the shorter workload. There are two probability distributions, F_l and F_r, and a customer's service time has distribution F_l if it is served by its left server and F_r otherwise.
The conjecture is: even in simple queueing systems, the stability conditions may depend both on the initial values and on the whole distribution of the driving sequences.

accepted.question_text: Consider an open polling system with two stations and two heterogeneous servers. Each station has Poisson input of rate 1. For i, j in {1, 2}, service times of server j at station i are i.i.d. exponential with rate mu_i^(j). Both servers use the exhaustive service policy, switch-over times are zero, and a server becomes passive if neither station has a free customer. In the positive four-dimensional parameter cube for {(mu_i^(j))}, does the subset of parameter values for which the system is null recurrent have positive Lebesgue measure?
accepted.context_brief: Positive-measure null recurrence in polling system

evidence.quote: Consider an open polling system with two stations and two heterogeneous servers. Each station i = 1, 2 has a Poisson input with intensity lambda_i = 1. For i, j in {1, 2}, service times of server j at station i are i.i.d. exponential with intensity mu_i^(j). Both servers follow the so-called exhaustive service policy.
The system is characterised by 4 parameters {mu_i^(j)}_{i,j=1,2}.
The conjecture here is: in the positive 4-dimensional cube, the set of parameters {mu_i^(j)} for which the system is null-recurrent has a positive Lebesgue measure.

accepted.question_text: Consider a slotted multi-access channel in which packets have unit service time, arrivals during each slot are Poisson with parameter lambda, W_n is the number of packets in the system at the beginning of slot n, and each packet attempts transmission in slot n with probability p_n. A transmission succeeds if exactly one packet transmits, collides if two or more transmit, and is empty if none transmits. Suppose p_{n+1} may depend only on p_n and on the binary information of whether slot n contained a successful transmission. Does there exist a protocol of this form for which the Markov chain (W_n, p_n) is positive recurrent for some lambda > 0?

evidence.quote: Consider a single channel which is shared among many users and transmits packets of a single length. Assume that time is slotted and each service time is equal to the slot length. The number of packages arriving into the system during a time slot is Poisson with parameter lambda.

At the beginning of time slot n, each package is trying to be transmitted with the same probability p_n independently of everything else. If two or more packages try to transmit simultaneously, the transmissions collide and packages stay in the system and have to try again later. If there is only one transmission, then it is successful and the package leaves the system. If there are no transmissions, then the slot is empty. Denote by W_n the number of packages in the system at the beginning of nth time slot.

Assume that probabilities p_n are defined inductively and that p_{n+1} may depend only on p_n and the binary information of whether there is a successful transmission in slot n or not. Then the pairs (W_n, p_n) form a time homogeneous Markov chain. The open question is: in the class of procedures described above, does there exist a protocol which makes the Markov chain (W_n, p_n) positive recurrent (ergodic), for some positive lambda?
